title: License-segregated foundation-model baseline (labeled, optional)
context: Several foundation models for computational pathology (e.g. UNI, CONCH) use non-commercial or gated weights licenses. Including a foundation-model baseline adds useful comparison data for researchers, but it must be clearly segregated and labeled as non-commercial if its weights are non-commercial/gated, and must never be required to use the benchmark (the permissive MIT-licensed path must stand alone). This is an optional M3 task; if included, the foundation model must be reported with the same honest provenance as other baselines. Heavy GPU runs become funded tasks with a fundedBudgetUsd cap. Domain-reviewer and license-reviewer sign-off required. See PLAN.md (Baselines, Non-commercial assets).
objective: Implement an optional license-segregated foundation-model baseline: record the weights license for the chosen encoder (e.g. UNI, CONCH, or equivalent); if the license is non-commercial or gated, clearly label it as such and place it in an explicitly segregated path (e.g. baselines/non-commercial/); ensure it is never a required dependency to use the benchmark. Report with the same honest provenance as pathology-image-benchmarks-baseline-001 (split ID, seeds, variance, preprocessing hash, compute provenance). Write a model card noting the non-commercial/gated weights license. Heavy GPU runs are scoped as a separate funded task.
acceptanceCriteria: The foundation model encoder's weights license is recorded in the model card and the allow-list/segregation record.

If the weights license is non-commercial or gated, the baseline is clearly labeled non-commercial and placed in a segregated path (e.g. baselines/non-commercial/); it is never required to use the benchmark.
A permissive (MIT-licensed) baseline path exists independently and is not dependent on this optional baseline.
Results are reported with the same honest provenance as other baselines: split ID, seed(s), across-seed variance, preprocessing hash, and compute provenance.
A model card is shipped: intended use = research benchmarking only (not clinical), weights license and any usage-agreement requirements stated, metrics with variance, known limitations.
Domain-reviewer and license-reviewer sign-off are recorded in the governance log.
Heavy GPU training is identified as a separate funded task (not part of this donated-lane deliverable beyond code + lightweight run).
output: An optional license-segregated foundation-model baseline PR with a model card, weights-license record, segregated path, and honest provenance reporting; or a documented decision not to include this baseline.
